title: Geometry of Divergence: Tracking Hidden-State Trajectories for Adaptive Multi-Turn Reasoning (Liang, Yu, Nasiri, Garraghan; Lancaster / Huddersfield; arXiv 2608.30650v1, 31 Aug 2026)
sections_read: 4.1 Experimental Setup (Benchmarks, Models, Metrics, Implementation Details)
5 Probing Trajectory Divergence through Action Chains
5.2 Separability of Hidden-state Trajectories in Action Chains (Figure 4, Table 2)
6 Geometry-Triggered Adaptive Reasoning (Figure 5, Table 3; 'Applicability & Future Direction')
Note: the text refers to an Appendix ('full experimental setup are provided in the Appendix'), but no appendix is present in paper.txt (8 pages).

setup.task_and_data: Four multi-turn tasks: Math and Code from the sharded-prompt 'Lost in Conversation' framework (Laban et al. 2025); Airline and Retail from tau-Bench (tool-using customer-service agents). Binary episode correctness from benchmark ground truth. Math: n=259 correct vs 227 incorrect episodes (Fig. 3); other n not reported in text.
setup.models: Qwen3-14B and Qwen3-32B (thinking-mode toggle) and Llama-3.1-8B, used as both the agent and the user simulator. Only 6 task-model pairings: Math-Llama-3.1-8B, Code-Qwen3-14B, Retail/Airline x Qwen3-14B/32B. Inference with vLLM on 8 L40S + 4 H200.
setup.positions_layers: One hidden state per turn: final token of the user input q_t, at one fixed layer per model (layer 22 Qwen3-14B, 42 Qwen3-32B, 16 Llama-3.1-8B). Fig. 3 (Math) shows layers 20 and 24 instead.
setup.measures: Temporal curvature kappa_t = cosine between consecutive displacements v_t = h_t - h_{t-1} and v_{t-1}; variance slope beta_t = OLS slope of trace(Cov(h_0..h_lambda)) against prefix length. Both defined from turn 2.
setup.baselines: Trigger policies for turning on thinking mode: Never-think, Always-think, Warm-up (think on first two turns), action-conditioned (predicted next action; classifier F1 Read 0.826, Respond 0.711, Write 0.700, Transfer 0.531), geometry thresholds (kappa_t < tau or beta_t > tau), Learned-HST classifier on last three actions + (kappa, beta). 5 trials per task.
setup.controls: Turn alignment (index by turn rather than episode length); identical turn windows for both metrics; all non-Never policies share the Warm-up; Mann-Whitney U tests. No null model for kappa, no layer sweep beyond Fig. 3, no causal intervention on hidden states.

figures.what_is_plotted: Schematic: hidden states h0-h4 over turns 0-4 with a success trajectory (blue) and a failure trajectory (red), temporal curvature and variance slope annotated, action chain (Respond, Read, Write, Write, Respond) and 'Timing for Adaptive Reasoning' at turns 2-3.
figures.takeaway: Framing: failure trajectories bend and contract; intervene at the bend.

figures.what_is_plotted: (a) Box plots of per-episode mean kappa for correct vs incorrect episodes in six task-model pairings. (b) Mean and CI of variance slope beta_t, z-scored within task, with Mann-Whitney p-values.
figures.takeaway: Correct episodes have slightly higher kappa and higher beta; boxes overlap heavily.
figures.numbers: approx, read from figure: (a) medians correct/incorrect - Math (Llama-3.1-8B) -0.17/-0.235; Code (Qwen3-14B) +0.13/-0.055; Retail 14B -0.215/-0.24; Airline 14B -0.12/-0.17; Retail 32B -0.145/-0.185; Airline 32B -0.04/-0.125. (b) z-scored beta means correct/incorrect - Math +0.2/-0.2; Code +0.8/-0.48; Retail 14B +0.23/-0.14; Airline 14B +0.2 (CI crosses 0)/-0.06; Retail 32B +0.17/-0.13; Airline 32B +0.23/-0.05; p <.001, <.001, <.001, 0.30, <.001, 0.057.
figures.text_matches_figure: partly - direction matches the text (and Code correct median ~+0.13 matches +0.127), but panel (a) gives no significance tests for kappa and the per-episode distributions overlap heavily, so separation per episode is weak.

figures.what_is_plotted: Math task: turn-resolved kappa_t (top) and beta_t (bottom) for correct (n=259) vs incorrect (n=227) episodes at layers 20 and 24, turns 2-7, with CIs.
figures.takeaway: The gap opens gradually from turn 3-4 and widens; both groups' kappa becomes more negative with turn index.
figures.numbers: approx, read from figure: kappa at turn 2 ~-0.15 (L20) / -0.12 (L24) for both; turn 4 correct ~-0.27, incorrect ~-0.34; turn 6 correct ~-0.24, incorrect ~-0.36; incorrect turn 7 ~-0.41. beta L20: 22 -> 49 (correct, turn 6) vs 22 -> 45 (incorrect, turns 6-7); L24: 40 -> 88 vs 39 -> 78. Correct curves stop at turn 6.
figures.text_matches_figure: partly - supports the claims, but Section 3.2 says the probe layer for Llama-3.1-8B (the Math model in Fig. 2) is 16, while Fig. 3 shows layers 20 and 24 and does not name the model.

figures.what_is_plotted: (a, b) Effect size (AUC - 1/2) on curvature (x) vs variance slope (y) for each of the top-20 three-action chains in Retail and Airline, marked by significance; (c) 2-D PCA of hidden states for the Respond x3 chain at t+0, t+1, t+2 with group means, KDE and action centroids, plus the mean path.
figures.takeaway: Retail separation mostly via variance slope; Airline adds curvature; Respond x3 stands out.
figures.text_matches_figure: partly - (a)/(b) match the text; but in (c) correct episodes move into the region where incorrect episodes already sit and the two means coincide at t+2, which reads as convergence rather than correct episodes 'continuously expanding outwards'; the caption does not say which domain (c) is from.

figures.what_is_plotted: Top-20 three-action chains with correct/incorrect window shares (%) and per-domain frequency rank.
figures.takeaway: Read-heavy chains dominate both domains; Resp x3 is far more common in failed Airline episodes; Transfer-ending chains are more common in successful Airline episodes.

figures.what_is_plotted: Share of three-action chains containing each action, correct vs incorrect, with Delta = incorrect - correct.
figures.takeaway: Action mixes differ little in Retail but a lot in Airline (failed Airline episodes write more and transfer/read less).
figures.text_matches_figure: yes - note that in Airline the behaviour itself differs strongly between groups, so geometry differences there may partly reflect which actions were taken.

figures.what_is_plotted: Qwen3-14B, Retail (a) and Airline (b): task reward, database accuracy and read accuracy for fixed, action-conditioned, geometry and learned trigger policies.
figures.takeaway: Timing matters more than total thinking; geometry and learned triggers are near the top on reward.
figures.numbers: approx, read from figure: Retail reward Never 0.286, Always 0.307, Warm-up 0.361, Read 0.393, Write 0.381, Transfer ~0.353, Respond 0.290, kappa 0.397, beta 0.393, Learned 0.398; DB accuracy ~0.39-0.49 (spread 9.8%); read accuracy ~0.735-0.765 (spread 3.1%). Airline reward 0.196, 0.356, 0.348, 0.352, 0.340, ~0.29, 0.372, 0.384, 0.392, 0.420; DB accuracy ~0.26-0.50 (spread 23.9%); read accuracy ~0.54-0.65 (spread 11.3%), lowest (~0.565) under geometry/learned triggers.
figures.text_matches_figure: yes for reward values; the drop in Airline read accuracy under geometry triggers is not discussed.

figures.what_is_plotted: Task reward (top) and mean token cost in thousands with max-turn terminations (bottom) for six policies in four domain-model settings.
figures.takeaway: Geometry triggers give good reward at the lowest token cost; Learned-HST is best or tied in 3 of 4 rows.
figures.text_matches_figure: partly - the headline average of 0.396 equals the per-row best of the two geometry triggers (reader's arithmetic: (0.397+0.392+0.442+0.352)/4 = 0.396); each trigger alone averages 0.381 (beta) and 0.394 (kappa); thresholds were picked by sweep; against the Warm-up policy that all triggers include (average 0.3485), the gain is about +0.05, not +0.155.

key_results.claim: Two trajectory statistics separate correct from incorrect episodes before the episode ends.
key_results.quote: Across four tasks and three underlying LLMs, we observed that these geometric signals distinguish between correct and incorrect episodes prior to completion.

key_results.claim: Failed episodes have lower (more negative) mean curvature in all six pairings; the gaps are small.
key_results.quote: with differences (Correct−Incorrect) of: Math +0.047, Code +0.148, Retail (14B) +0.030, Airline (14B) +0.049, Retail (32B) +0.035, Airline (32B) +0.088

key_results.claim: Correct episodes have higher variance slope; not significant in Airline.
key_results.quote: Separability is significant for all pairings except the two Airline cases (14B p=0.30, 32B p=0.057)

key_results.claim: Episode length is a direct confound for both statistics.
key_results.quote: incorrect episodes are systematically longer than successful ones due to retries, stalls, and back-and-forth entanglement, and a longer trajectory is mechanically more curved and accumulates more variance regardless of correctness

key_results.claim: Separability depends on action type: output chains separate, acquisition chains do not.
key_results.quote: information-output chains carrying the strongest discriminative structure while information-acquisition chains carry little

key_results.claim: Averaged over four settings, geometry-triggered thinking raises reward from 0.241 (Never-think) to 0.396.
key_results.quote: Averaging over the four settings, the geometry-conditioned trigger raises task reward from 0.241 under Never-thinking to 0.396

key_results.claim: A single curvature threshold ties the trained classifier at lower token cost.
key_results.quote: κ < −0.20 ties Learned-HST on Retail 14B (0.397 vs 0.398) at lower token cost (101.0k vs 104.4k)

key_results.claim: Thinking only on the first two turns already beats always thinking in some settings.
key_results.quote: On Qwen3-32B, Warm-up achieves 0.405 compared with 0.384 for Always-thinking, while using 12.2k fewer tokens

key_results.claim: Action-conditioned triggers do not transfer across domains.
key_results.quote: the most effective action does not transfer across domains

key_results.claim: Hidden states are read at one fixed intermediate layer per model, at the last user-input token.
key_results.quote: taken from a fixed intermediate probe layer (layer 22 for Qwen3-14B, layer 42 for Qwen3-32B, and layer 16 for Llama-3.1-8B)

methods.name: Temporal curvature kappa_t
methods.what_it_measures: Cosine between consecutive displacement vectors of the hidden state across turns (three-point statistic); negative = the update reverses the previous update.
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: Direction 3 (jump vs drift): abrupt reversal vs gradual change. In a multi-turn pushback setting, a reversal right after the user's pushback turn could mark an override-like event (fate 4), but the paper does not test this.
methods.causal_followup_it_allows: None in the paper; one could patch the pre-reversal state into the post-reversal turn and see if the answer is restored.
methods.data_and_compute_needed: One hidden state per turn at one layer; negligible compute beyond inference.

methods.name: Variance slope beta_t
methods.what_it_measures: OLS slope of the trace of the prefix covariance of turn states vs prefix length (spread grows or contracts).
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: Weak: contraction ('premature convergence') might accompany locking onto a wrong answer; not fate-specific.

methods.name: Turn alignment
methods.what_it_measures: Index states by turn and compute both statistics on identical turn windows to reduce length confounds.
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: Control for any trajectory/fork-point comparison (flipped vs resisted).

methods.name: Action-chain conditioning with AUC - 1/2 effect sizes
methods.what_it_measures: Separability of correct vs incorrect windows within each three-action chain type.
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: Analog: stratify flipped vs resisted items by what the model just did (e.g., restated own answer vs deferred) before comparing geometry.

methods.name: Geometry-triggered intervention (threshold kappa_t < tau -> enable thinking)
methods.what_it_measures: Whether an online geometric signal can decide when to spend extra deliberation.
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: Not a diagnostic; a monitor-to-fix pattern (Stage B-style inference-time fix).
methods.data_and_compute_needed: 5 trials per task per policy on tau-Bench; threshold sweep.

methods.name: 2-D PCA trajectory plots with group means and KDE
methods.what_it_measures: Visual position of correct vs incorrect states over three turns.

controls_worth_copying: Turn (position) alignment so that trajectory statistics are compared at matched indices, with both statistics defined on identical windows.
Give every intervention policy the same warm-up so comparisons isolate the trigger (they did this; the headline then compared against the policy without it).
Stratify by action/behaviour type before claiming geometric separability.
Report token cost alongside accuracy for inference-time fixes.

pitfalls.pitfall: Length confound acknowledged by the authors; turn alignment does not fully remove it, because per-episode means still average over more (and later, more negative-kappa) turns in longer incorrect episodes (Fig. 3 shows kappa falls with turn index for both groups).
pitfalls.quote: incorrect episodes are systematically longer than successful ones due to retries, stalls, and back-and-forth entanglement, and a longer trajectory is mechanically more curved and accumulates more variance regardless of correctness

pitfalls.pitfall: Headline baseline is Never-think, but every geometry trigger includes the Warm-up; the fair comparison is Warm-up (average ~0.349 by reader's arithmetic), which shrinks the gain to ~+0.05.
pitfalls.quote: To keep the comparison controlled, every method except Never-thinking adopts this same Warm-up.

pitfalls.pitfall: Thresholds are chosen by sweeping on the same evaluation, and the 0.396 average takes the better of two triggers per row.
pitfalls.quote: Sweeping τκ is unimodal with an optimum locatable by a one-dimensional scan

pitfalls.pitfall: No null for curvature: if turn states jitter around a fixed point, consecutive displacement cosines are negative by construction (about -0.5 for i.i.d. jitter; reader's calculation), so negative kappa need not mean a 'reversal' of reasoning.
Signals are task-dependent and do not transfer universally (authors, about prior hidden-state signals and their own variance slope).
pitfalls.quote: these signals do not transfer universally across tasks, which is consistent with the task-dependent behavior we observe for the variance slope

pitfalls.pitfall: The same LLM plays the user simulator, so 'user' turns are model-generated.
pitfalls.quote: as the core components of both the assistant agent and the user simulator

pitfalls.pitfall: One layer per model, last user token only; Fig. 3 uses layers 20 and 24, inconsistent with the stated layer 16 for Llama-3.1-8B; no layer sweep or component analysis.
Purely correlational: no intervention on hidden states; the 'fix' acts on behaviour (thinking mode).
Small effect sizes (AUC - 1/2 at most ~0.22) and heavy overlap of per-episode distributions (Fig. 2a).
2-D PCA interpretation ('expands outwards') is not what the plotted means show (they converge at t+2).
pitfalls.quote: the scatter of incorrect episode remains in the bottom-right region of the Respond cluster throughout, showing no significant spatial expansion

limitations_quote: these signals do not transfer universally across tasks, which is consistent with the task-dependent behavior we observe for the variance slope
limitations_note: No dedicated limitations section; this is the closest explicit statement. The paper also says Warm-up 'does not perform consistently across settings' and that action-conditioned triggers need the error distribution 'identified in advance'.
future_work_quote: trajectory geometry provides a new lens on multi-turn adversarial attacks, which is an active area in which jailbreaks are spread across turns to divert an agent away from its objective

bears_on_fates.how: Gives two cheap turn-level statistics and shows (Fig. 3) a gradual widening of the correct/incorrect gap from turn 3-4, i.e. drift rather than a single jump, in one task; no causal test.
A curvature reversal at a pushback turn could be a candidate override signature in multi-turn pushback, but the paper studies episode outcomes, not knowledge-vs-action conflicts.
Variance contraction in failures is loosely compatible with information loss, but no decoding of task information is done.
Nothing: no probes for correctness information, no ablation or patching.

bears_on_group_angle: Helps a little: it treats each episode as a path of hidden states and compares groups of paths (correct vs incorrect) with simple path statistics (consecutive-step cosine, growth of the point-cloud spread), plus turn alignment. For our token-path / fork-point idea these are cheap baselines to beat. Warns: path statistics are confounded by path length and by index (kappa drifts with turn index for everyone), need a null (stationary jitter gives negative kappa), should be checked across layers, and 2-D PCA pictures can tell the opposite story from the text. It uses no subspaces, principal angles, RSA/CKA or causal tests.
architecture_location: Only 'where' information: one intermediate residual layer per model, final user-input token - layer 22 of 40 in Qwen3-14B (~55% depth), 42 of 64 in Qwen3-32B (~66%), 16 of 32 in Llama-3.1-8B (50%); Fig. 3 shows similar patterns at layers 20 and 24. No head/MLP-level analysis. The direction of the effect is the same in all six task-model pairings, but the design is only partly crossed (Llama only on Math, Qwen3-32B only on tau-Bench).
actionable_fix: Training-free inference-time monitor: when turn-to-turn curvature drops below a threshold, switch on extra deliberation (thinking mode). Gains over a two-turn warm-up are modest (~+0.05 reward, reader's arithmetic) with lower token cost. For our project it suggests a Stage B 'inference-time' fix arm: trigger a re-check of the model's own earlier answer when the representation shows a reversal after pushback, to compare against fate-matched fixes and DPO.
reuse_verdict: adapt (light) - copy turn/position alignment and the kappa/beta statistics as cheap baselines for direction 3 and for the fork-point analysis; avoid interpreting negative curvature as reversal without a null, the Never-think headline comparison, and per-row best-of selection.
relevance_to_project: Low to moderate. It is about multi-turn agent episodes with outcome labels, not about correctness information that the model acts against; there are no probes, no causal tests, and only one layer per model. Its only real use for us is direction 3 (jump vs drift) and as a cheap trajectory baseline plus a monitor-to-intervention pattern for Stage B. Less relevant than its title suggests.
